# Geometry Shader Processing

Also called: Geometry Shader Voxelization, GS-based Voxel Rendering

## Overview
Geometry Shader Processing is a family of GPU-based techniques that generate voxel geometry or volumetric visualizations dynamically from primitive inputs (points, triangles) within the graphics pipeline. It solves the problem of rendering volumetric data without pre-computing and storing full mesh geometry for every voxel on the CPU or in static buffers [S1, S2, S3, unofficial]. Unlike [Voxels rasterized as geometry](27-voxels-rasterized-as-geometry.md) which may use instancing or display lists, this family relies on the Geometry Shader (GS) to expand input primitives into voxel shells, slices, or billboards at runtime. It differs from [Binary Volume Rendering (Opacity Thresholding)](1015-binary-volume-rendering-opacity-thresholding.md) by explicitly generating geometry rather than thresholding textures, and from [Naive Voxel Rendering](1103-naive-voxel-rendering.md) by utilizing GPU-side expansion logic.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on the principle of primitive expansion within the Geometry Shader stage. The core mechanism involves receiving a stream of input primitives (typically `GL_POINTS` or `GL_TRIANGLES`) and emitting a stream of output primitives (typically `GL_TRIANGLE_STRIP` or `GL_LINES`) that represent the voxelized or volumetric structure.

Key shared characteristics include:
1.  **Dynamic Generation:** Geometry is not stored in vertex buffers but computed per-vertex/per-primitive in the GS.
2.  **Input Abstraction:** Inputs are simplified primitives (points or triangles) that carry minimal data (position, flags, or attributes), offloading the complexity of voxel topology to the shader.
3.  **Matrix Utilization:** Most methods utilize the Model-View-Projection (MVP) matrix to transform local voxel offsets into clip space, ensuring correct perspective and view-dependent culling [S2, S3, unofficial].
4.  **Output Primitives:** The output is always rasterizable geometry (quads, lines, or strips) that integrates with the standard rasterization pipeline.

## Subtopics

### [Geometry Shader Cube Expansion](1074-geometry-shader-cube-expansion.md)
Converts input triangles or points into a voxel shell representation by expanding each input into a cube of 6 faces. It differs from [Geometry Shader (Quads)](4369-geometry-shader-quads.md) by storing a single point per voxel with face flags, generating all 6 faces dynamically, whereas Quads stores one face per primitive. Choose this when rendering a voxelized mesh surface where interior filling is not required.

### [Velocity Visualization via Geometry Shader Extrusion](1581-velocity-visualization-via-geometry-shader-extrusion.md)
Visualizes velocity vectors on a structured grid by extruding points into line segments based on sampled 3D volume data. It differs from particle-based methods by operating on a grid and using the GS to link start and end points. Choose this for flow field visualization where vector magnitude and direction need to be mapped to line length and orientation.

### [Geometry Shader Triangle Slicing (Z-Pass)](1681-geometry-shader-triangle-slicing-z-pass.md)
Performs multi-channel surface voxelization by clipping input triangles against volume slice boundaries within the GS, emitting valid fragments for specific volume layers. It differs from [Pixel Shader Fragment Clipping](1685-pixel-shader-fragment-clipping.md) by performing clipping in the GS, avoiding fragment rejection overhead. Choose this for Z-pass volume rendering where triangles must be sliced into discrete depth layers.

### [Geometry Shader (Quads)](4369-geometry-shader-quads.md)
Renders voxels by generating one quad per face, where each input point represents a single face. It differs from [Geometry Shader Processing](2524-geometry-shader-processing.md) (Cube Expansion) by outputting 4 vertices per primitive instead of 12, reducing buffer space but requiring one input point per face. Choose this when memory bandwidth is a constraint and face-level control is needed.

### [GPU Particle Rendering via Geometry Shader](4444-gpu-particle-rendering-via-geometry-shader.md)
Generates 2D sprite quads from point primitives for efficient particle rendering. It differs from CPU-instanced rendering by offloading vertex expansion to the GPU. Choose this for particle systems requiring dynamic per-particle size and color manipulation without CPU-side mesh generation.

## Background
The use of Geometry Shaders for voxelization emerged as a method to bypass the CPU bottleneck of generating voxel meshes for large datasets. Early implementations focused on converting triangle meshes into voxel shells for real-time rendering [S1, S2, S3, unofficial]. The technique has since expanded to include velocity visualization [S1, unofficial] and multi-channel surface voxelization [S1, unofficial]. It is primarily used in real-time graphics applications where dynamic voxel generation is preferred over static storage, such as in scientific visualization and interactive 3D modeling tools.
